Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third
one made me the most (A)(confident / nervous):
changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept
the same hairstyle because I had been worried
about my forehead. I had always thought it was
large, and I didn’t want to draw attention to it.
Since I was feeling (B)(anxious / confident) after the
first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and
talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns
and helped me find a shorter hairstyle that suited
me.
The next day at school, my classmates were a bit
surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I
realized that trying a different look wasn’t as
difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made
me feel more confident about myself. I didn’t
expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would
have such a (C)(positive / negative) effect on how I
felt about myself.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

solution: (A) wanted의 목적어 us에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리이며, want 는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취해 ‘want+목적어+목적격보어(to 부정사)(~가 …하기를 원하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 동사이므 로, to부정사인 to start가 알맞다. (B) 문장의 동사로 gave가 있으므로 준동사 자리이며, 뒤에 목 적어인 재귀대명사 ourselves를 취하여 능동 관계를 나타내면 서, 흐름상 ‘도전할’이라는 의미로 앞의 명사구 an assignment (과제)를 수식해야 하므로 형용사적 용법의 to부정사인 to challenge가 알맞다. (C) was의 보어 자리에 쓰였으며, 뒤에 온 대명사 something 을 목적어로 취해야 하므로, 동명사 trying이 알맞다.

solution: (A) 접속사 while(~하는 동안) 뒤에 주어(I)와 be동사(was)가 생 략되고 분사만 남은 형태의 부사절 축약 구문으로, 생략된 주 어 I가 ‘하고 있었던’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어로 대명사 them이 이어지므로, 생략된 was와 함께 능동의 과거진행형(was/were+-ing) 을 이루는 현재분사 doing이 알맞다. (B) 뒤에 이어지는 완전한 절(it took ~ ocean)이 앞의 추상명사구 the fact(사실)의 구체적 내용이므로, 동격 접속사 that이 알맞다. Host: On today’s show, we are going to learn about
special park benches in Zimbabwe ⓐwhere
are called Friendship Benches. We have two
special guests. First, please welcome the
founder of the Friendship Bench program, Dr.
Dixon Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired
you to come up with the program?
Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience
ⓑwhich I had as a psychiatrist. One of my
patients had become severely depressed. However,
she couldn’t get help ⓒbecause she was unable
to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This
shocked me, as I had never considered ⓓsuch a
problem before. In fact, it is difficult for many
people in Zimbabwe to pay for transportation and

Host: On today’s show, we are going to learn about
special park benches in Zimbabwe called
Friendship Benches. We have two special
guests. First, please welcome the founder of
the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon
Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you
to come up with the program?
Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience
I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients
had become severely depressed. (A)______________,
she couldn’t get help because she was unable
to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This
shocked me, as I had never considered such
a
problem
before.
(B)______________,
it
is
difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay
for
transportation
and
receive
medical
treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack
of psychiatrists in the country for many years.
When the Friendship Bench program started
in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists
serving Zimbabwe’s population of over twelve
million people. I needed to find a way to
bring psychiatry into the community.
Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could
you explain to us how the Friendship Bench
program works?
Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as
a way to provide accessible mental health
services. It offers talk therapy sessions to
people dealing with issues such as depression
or anxiety. The sessions are free and are
provided by respected elderly women from
the
community.
These
women,
called
“grandmothers,” volunteer to sit with patients
at the benches, listen to their stories, and
provide them with emotional support.
Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing
grandmothers become a part of your program?
Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our
program because they are deeply connected
to the community. (C)______________, they have
all the qualities of a counselor, such as
excellent listening skills, empathy, and the
ability to engage in meaningful discussions.
They are also very reliable, which is important
for our efforts to support mental health. At
the beginning, we started with only fourteen
volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are
thousands of grandmothers who have been
trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in
Zimbabwe.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Host: That’s very kind of you. Can you tell us about
your experience as a grandmother for the
Friendship Bench program?
Grandma Moyo: It’s been wonderful. Seeking help
for mental health problems is nothing to be
ashamed of. I’ve seen how it can make a
difference in people’s lives. One patient of
mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going
through a difficult time after her mom passed
away. I counseled her and helped her begin
her recovery journey. Now her life is back on
track, and she has even started her own
business! Cases like this make me so proud
to be part of the program. It is such a
rewarding experience to help people make
positive changes in their lives.

Host: On today’s show, we are going to learn about
special park benches in Zimbabwe called
Friendship Benches. We have two special
guests. First, please welcome the founder of
the Friendship Bench program, Dr. Dixon
Chibanda. Can you tell us what inspired you
to come up with the program?
Dr. Chibanda: Sure. The idea came from an experience
I had as a psychiatrist. One of my patients
had become severely depressed. (A)______________,
she couldn’t get help because she was unable
to afford the bus ride to the hospital. This
shocked me, as I had never considered such
a
problem
before.
(B)______________,
it
is
difficult for many people in Zimbabwe to pay
for
transportation
and
receive
medical
treatment. Furthermore, there has been a lack
of psychiatrists in the country for many years.
When the Friendship Bench program started
in 2006, there were only eleven psychiatrists
serving Zimbabwe’s population of over twelve
million people. I needed to find a way to
bring psychiatry into the community.
Host: Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could
you explain to us how the Friendship Bench
program works?
Dr. Chibanda: Certainly. The program was created as
a way to provide accessible mental health
services. It offers talk therapy sessions to
people dealing with issues such as depression
or anxiety. The sessions are free and are
provided by respected elderly women from
the
community.
These
women,
called
“grandmothers,” volunteer to sit with patients
at the benches, listen to their stories, and
provide them with emotional support.
Host: What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing
grandmothers become a part of your program?
Dr. Chibanda: Grandmothers were chosen for our
program because they are deeply connected
to the community. (C)______________, they have
all the qualities of a counselor, such as
excellent listening skills, empathy, and the
ability to engage in meaningful discussions.
They are also very reliable, which is important
for our efforts to support mental health. At
the beginning, we started with only fourteen
volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are
thousands of grandmothers who have been
trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in
Zimbabwe.

윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Dr. Chibanda had a patient who couldn’t takethe bus to the hospital due to severe mentalproblems.

serving Zimbabwe’s population of over twelve
million people. I needed to find a way to
bring psychiatry into the community.

Thanks to streaming platforms, you can watch your favorite shows anytime. You can even watch a whole series without stopping! This is called binge-watching. It sounds fun, but binge-watching isn’t good for you. It can cause sleep problems and lead to reduced physical activity. So, how can you prevent binge-watching from affecting your health? First, decide how long you are going to watch a show before you start, and set an alarm. When the alarm goes off, it’s important to stop watching even if you are in the middle of the show. of
miles
away.

In the 19th century, the Industrial Revolution led
to a dramatic increase in factory production in the
United States. The demand for workers increased,
and many new positions were filled by children. By
1900, about twenty percent of all children in the
United States were employed, and some of those
working in factories were only four years old. The
work was difficult and ⓐdangerous, leaving many
child laborers with health problems.
Factory owners ⓑturned to child labor for several
reasons. For example, children could be paid less
than adult workers. They were also less likely to go
on strike.
Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, wanted
to reveal how cruel this system was. So he quit his
teaching job and started to work for the National
Child
Labor
Committee
as
an
investigative
photographer. He gained access to factories by
pretending to have different jobs like insurance
agent or fire inspector.
Once inside, he would ⓒphotograph the children
working there. He would also ask their names and
ages and record information about their living and
working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he secretly
gathered information and took photographs to
expose factory owners who were ⓓtaking advantage
of helpless children.
Hine’s photographs captured young children doing
all sorts of jobs. These included picking vegetables,
weaving baskets, and even handling dangerous
equipment. What is more, the children’s faces
showed the tragic impact of hard labor. When
people saw the children’s joyless expressions, they
ⓔcould not help but feel heartbroken.
The pictures were later shown in exhibitions,
lectures, magazine articles, and so on. As a result,
the public realized just how serious the situation
was. Soon, many states passed stronger laws (A)____
_________________________________________. In 1938, the

to a dramatic increase in factory production in the
United States. The (A)[demand / supply] for workers
increased, and many new positions were filled by
children. By 1900, about twenty percent of all
children in the United States were employed, and
some of those working in factories ⓐwere only four
years old. The work was difficult and dangerous,
leaving many child laborers with health problems.
Factory owners turned to child labor for several
reasons. For example, children could be paid less
than adult workers. They were also (B)[likely /
unlikely] to go on strike.
Lewis Hine, a teacher and photographer, ⓑwanted
to reveal how cruel this system was. So he quit his
teaching job and started to work for the National
Child
Labor
Committee
as
an
investigative
photographer. He gained access to factories by
pretending to have different jobs like insurance
agent or fire inspector.
Once inside, he would photograph the children
working there. He would also ask their names and
ages and ⓒrecord information about their living
and working conditions. From 1908 to 1912, he
secretly gathered information and took photographs
to
expose
factory
owners
who
were
taking
advantage of (C)[helpless / competent] children.
Hine’s photographs captured young children doing
all sorts of jobs. These included picking vegetables,
weaving baskets, and even handling dangerous
equipment. What is more, the children’s faces
showed the tragic impact of hard labor. When
people saw the children’s joyless expressions, they
could not help but ⓓfeel heartbroken.
The pictures were later shown in exhibitions,
lectures, magazine articles, and so on. As a result,
the public realized just ⓔwhat serious the situation

In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along
the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This
industrial growth provided ⓐsteady jobs to people
in the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories
started dumping large amounts of waste into the
river. Although the river became polluted, most
people simply ⓑregarded this as a sign of the
area’s economic success.
In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The
likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train,
which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge.
At that time, few people in Cleveland cared. This
was because fires had been recorded on the
Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of
them had been much worse.
However, it wasn’t long before the 1969 fire
became famous. This was thanks to an article
published in Time magazine that year. The article
ⓒfeatured a shocking photograph of flames and
smoke rising from the river. But (A)이것은 1969년
화재의 사진이 아니었는데, 그것은 너무 빨리 진압되
어 아무도 그것의 사진을 찍지 못했다. In fact, it was
a picture of a much worse fire that had occurred
on the river several years earlier. Still, the image
had a great impact on people.
Around that time, the ⓓattitudes of Americans
toward environmental problems were starting to
change. More and more people were becoming
aware of the need to protect the environment, and
the shocking image of the burning river sparked
public anger about water pollution. As a result, the
Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a symbol of
pollution. A national environmental ⓔawareness
event was held on April 22, 1970, which later
became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972,
national water quality standards were established
with the passage of the Clean Water Act.

body:
In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along
the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This
industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in
the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started
dumping large amounts of waste into the river.
Although the river became polluted, most people
simply regarded this as a sign of the area’s
economic success.
In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The
likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train,
which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge.
At that time, few people in Cleveland cared. This
was because fires had been recorded on the
Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of
them had been much worse.
However, it wasn’t long before the 1969 fire
became famous. This was thanks to an article
(A)[published / publishing] in Time magazine that
year. The article featured a shocking photograph of
flames and smoke rising from the river. But this
was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which
(B)[put out / was put out] so quickly that nobody
took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a
much worse fire that had occurred on the river
several years earlier. Still, the image had a great
impact on people.
Around that time, the attitudes of Americans
toward environmental problems were starting to
change. More and more people were becoming
aware of the need to protect the environment, and
the shocking image of the burning river sparked
public anger about water pollution. As a result, the
Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a symbol of
pollution. A national environmental awareness event
was held on April 22, 1970, (C)[that / which] later
became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972,
national water quality standards were established
with the passage of the Clean Water Act.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 수식을 받는 an article이 ‘출판되어진’의 의미로 수동의 관 계이므로 과거분사 published가 적절하다 (B) the 1969 fire를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대 명사 다음에 오는 동사 자리이며, the 1969 fire가 ‘진압되는’ 대상으로 수동의 관계이므로 was put out이 적절하다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤에 이어져 선행사인 April 22, 1970을 부연 설명하 는 관계사절을 이루고 있으며 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절이 이어지므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. that은 계속적 용법으로는 쓸 수 없다. 참고로 ‘1970년 4월 22일 에 열린 전국적인 환경 의식 행사’가 제1회 지구의 날로 자리 잡 은 것이므로 보아, 앞 절 전체(A national environmental ~ on April 22, 1970)를 선행사로 볼 수도 있다.)

In the 1880s, industry began to grow rapidly along
the Cuyahoga River in the city of Cleveland. This
industrial growth provided steady jobs to people in
the area. Meanwhile, steel mills and factories started
dumping large amounts of waste into the river.
Although the river became polluted, most people
simply regarded this as a sign of the area’s
economic success.
In June 1969, the polluted river caught fire. The
likely cause was a burning flare falling from a train,
which set fire to oil-soaked waste beneath a bridge.
At that time, few people in Cleveland cared. This
was because fires had been recorded on the
Cuyahoga more than ten times before, and some of
them had been much worse.
However, it wasn’t long before the 1969 fire
became famous. This was thanks to an article
(A)[published / publishing] in Time magazine that
year. The article featured a shocking photograph of
flames and smoke rising from the river. But this
was not a photograph of the 1969 fire, which
(B)[put out / was put out] so quickly that nobody
took a picture of it. In fact, it was a picture of a
much worse fire that had occurred on the river
several years earlier. Still, the image had a great
impact on people.
Around that time, the attitudes of Americans
toward environmental problems were starting to
change. More and more people were becoming
aware of the need to protect the environment, and
the shocking image of the burning river sparked
public anger about water pollution. As a result, the
Cuyahoga River fire of 1969 became a symbol of
pollution. A national environmental awareness event
was held on April 22, 1970, (C)[that / which] later
became known as the first Earth Day. And in 1972,
national water quality standards were established
with the passage of the Clean Water Act.

Shortly after we started the band, a global
pandemic* began. Since all of our normal lives were
put on hold, we valued our online ⓐinteractions
more than ever. At one point, Singaporean Sam
became ill and needed to spend some time in the
hospital, so the band ⓑtook a break.

as his birthday present. When we played it for him,
he laughed so hard that he cried. That was mainly
because the song was (A)[singing / sung] by the worst
singer in the band — me! It was good to see him
laugh even though he was lying in his hospital bed.
After Singaporean Sam ⓔrecovered, we decided
(B)[writing and recording / to write and record] our

Friendship,” and we posted it online. The song didn’t

*pandemic 전 세계적인 유행병

(C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ together)을 이끌며 선행사 the thing이 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고 로, the thing(s) which는 ’~하는 것’이라는 뜻으로, 선행사 the thing(s)을 포함한 관계대명사 what으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다.

Having many friends isn’t always best. Building
close friendships takes time, and the people you
spend the most time with often become good
friends. They know what you are really like and let
you be yourself, so you don’t have to try to
impress them. 이런 친구들은 당신을 이해할 뿐만 아
니라, 그들은 당신을 진심으로 소중하게 여깁니다.
Therefore, instead of always trying to make more
new friends, think about what you can do to value

We tried to practice once a week through a video
chat app, but we encountered several problems.
First of all, we all lived in different time zones. 이것
은 모두가 연습하기에 편한 시간을 고르는 것을 어렵
게 했다. Secondly, there were audio issues with the
app, which caused us to be out of sync. So we put
our heads together and devised a better way of
playing music. We decided to assemble the songs
as if we were working in a virtual music factory.
After we decided on a song, I would play it on
my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam. He
would sing along with the keyboard and send the
recording to American Sam. Then American Sam
would add his guitar part, and Samantha would
finish the song with her drumming.
When it came to choosing songs to play, we took
turns. Since each of us prefers a different genre of
music and comes from a different culture, we all
ended up learning a lot about different kinds of
music. It was interesting and a lot of fun.

how our virtual band overcame online challengesto make music together

close friendships takes time, and the people you

Lees?” To my surprise, all three eagerly agreed. That
was the start of our band’s journey.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?

During World War II, there was a group of people
who ⓐrisked everything to protect priceless works
of art from ⓑruin. In 1943, around 345 people
from 14 different Allied nations* came together to
form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and ⓒArchives (MFAA)
program. They were not trained soldiers but scholars
and ⓓexperts of various kinds, such as professors,
historians, and architects. These brave men and
women ⓔvolunteered to protect Europe’s cultural
heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men.”
*Allied nations (1, 2차 세계대전 때의) 연합국
choices: ⓐ: to put something in a situation in which itcould be lost, destroyed, or harmed
ⓑ: the state or process of being destroyed orseverely damaged
ⓒ: a collection of historical documents or records ofa government, a family, a place, or an organization
ⓓ: a person with special knowledge, skills, ortraining in something
ⓔ: to do something while being forced to do so
solution: volunteer가 ‘자원하다’라는 뜻이며, 보기에 주어진 ‘to do something while being forced to do so(어떤 것을 강요당하면서 하다)’는 알맞은 설명이 아니므로, ‘to offer to do something without being forced or paid to do it(강요받지 않거나 돈을 받지 않 고 어떤 것을 하겠다고 제안하다)’으로 고쳐야 한다.

When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal
was ⓐto prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks.
The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not
to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other
culturally (A)[significant / insignificant] buildings. They
also visited areas that ⓑhave already been destroyed
to restore ⓒdamaged architecture and works of art.
ⓓIt wasn’t long before their role expanded. During
the war, the Nazis had been stealing works of art
and other cultural treasures from countries across
Europe. They hid these treasures in places ⓔlike
castles, mines, and caves. When the Monuments Men
learned about this, they (B)[started / gave up] looking
for the stolen treasures. Their search has since been
called “the greatest treasure hunt in history.”
When Germany began to ⓕlosing the war, the stolen
objects came under (C)[threat / protection]. Hitler
ordered his forces to destroy everything that could be
useful to the Allied armies before they retreated from
an area. Some Nazi leaders believed that this included
not just military and industrial equipment but
everything of value — even the stolen works of art.

centers, people from different ethnic backgrounds

people, the food reflects the wide range of
diversity within Singapore. Food traditions from
China, Malaysia, India, and other countries are
passed down.

dishes, we share our history and the unique

Reading and writing systems are different across
cultures. People from Western cultures read and
write from left to right, while those from some
Middle Eastern cultures read and write from right to
left. People from some Eastern cultures, like that of
Japan, read and write from top to bottom. Some
global
websites
take
these
differences
into
consideration and adjust their websites for people
in different regions. In countries where text is read
from right to left, the website’s search button is on
the left and the logo is on the right. If you visit
the same websites in a different language setting,
you will see a different format.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Imagine you have fallen down and broken your
right arm. There are some things that would be
(A)[easy / difficult] to do with your injured arm. For
example, you might not be able to carry heavy
boxes or ride your bike. What about accessing the
Internet? If you are right-handed, using a computer
mouse or touchscreen with your (B)[left / right]
hand would be awkward and take a lot of time.
However, this is a minor challenge compared to
what some of us face on the Internet. For people
with certain disabilities, many websites can be
(C)[possible / impossible] to use. This is the reason
why web accessibility is important. Web accessibility
is the practice of making sure that websites can be
used by everyone, including people with disabilities.
So what exactly makes a website accessible?
Here are some common features of accessible
websites.
(A)         (B)          (C)

(B) 당신이 오른손잡이라는 것을 가정하고 있으므로, 왼손으로 컴퓨터 마우스나 터치스크린을 사용하는 것이 어색하고 많은 시간이 걸릴 것이라는 흐름이 되는 left(왼쪽의)가 알맞다. W: Today, we’re talking with Daniel Smith, a
volunteer for the Big Buddy program. Welcome,
Daniel! (A)Could you explain the program to us?
M: Sure! It helps teenagers find adult mentors. Its
purpose is to encourage supportive relationships
between mentors and teenagers. Also, through the
program, teenagers can develop their skills. I’m
currently mentoring a boy named Jason. He wants
help with his social skills, so we decided to join a
rock-climbing gym together. While we’re there, I
help Jason interact with the other climbers, and his
conversation skills are already improving. If this
sounds interesting to you, then I highly recommend
volunteering with the Big Buddy program.
W: I’m definitely interested. Not only does it benefit
the teenagers, but it also creates harmony
within the community.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: Can you provide more details about
solution: 밑줄 친 ‘Could you explain ~?’은 ‘~을 설명해 주겠니?’라는 뜻의 설 명을 요청하는 표현으로 ‘Can you describe ~?(~을 설명해 주겠니?)’, ‘Could you clarify ~?(~을 분명히 말해주겠니?)’, ‘Can you elaborate on ~?(~에 대해 자세히 설명해 주겠니?)’ 또는 ‘Can you provide more details about ~?(~에 대해 더 상세한 설명을 해주겠니?)’으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있다. 그러나 ❸ ‘Could you repeat ~?’은 ‘~을 한 번 더 말해주겠니?’라는 뜻의 반복을 요청하는 표현이므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

Color blindness is a common visual disability. (A)색
맹을 지닌 사람들은 몇몇 색들을 구별하는 것을 어렵
다고 여긴다. This can cause problems, especially
when graphs and charts only use colors to show
the
differences
between
sets
of
information.
Accessible websites use other indicators along with
the colors. For example, a line in green may also
be dotted, while a line in blue is solid. This ensures
that everyone can tell the two lines apart.
The accessibility features of websites don’t just
help people with disabilities. They can make online
experiences
easier
for
everyone,
regardless
of
abilities or situations. When websites are easy to
navigate and understand, we can all benefit from a
more inclusive online experience.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Having a visual disability doesn’t necessarily mean a
person can’t see at all. Some people, including many
elderly people, simply have poor eyesight. This makes
it (A)[easy / difficult] for them to read. For this reason,
accessible websites have a background color that
contrasts with the color of their text. This makes the
text (B)[clear / unclear] enough for most people to see.
As for audio content, accessible websites allow users
to adjust the volume of background sound or to turn
it off altogether. This gives users both with and
without hearing difficulties (C)[less / more] control
over their experience while they are using the sites.

G: Hey! Did you finish writing your research paper?
B: I did! I wrote about the “curb cut effect.”
G: What’s a curb cut?
B: It’s the part of the sidewalk that slopes down to
the street.
G: The part that connects the sidewalk to the road?
B: Yes. It was originally designed for wheelchair
users, but it benefits others, too.
G: (A)I’m surprised that it wasn’t originally designed
for everyone. I find curb cuts very helpful when I
ride my bike.
B: Right! Such changes made to help people with
disabilities often benefit everyone. People call
this the “curb cut effect”!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은?

body:
Reading and writing systems are different across
cultures. People from Western cultures read and
write from left to right, while those from some
Middle Eastern cultures read and write from right to
left. People from some Eastern cultures, like that of
Japan, read and write from top to bottom. Some
global
websites
take
these
differences
into
consideration and adjust their websites for people
in different regions. In countries where text is read
from right to left, the website’s search button is on
the left and the logo is on the right. If you visit
the same websites in a different language setting,
you will see a different format.

Reading and writing systems are different across cultures. People from some Eastern cultures, like that of Japan, read and write from top to bottom. Some global websites take these differences into consideration and adjust their websites for people in different regions. In countries where text is read from right to left, the website’s search button is on the left and the logo is on the right. If you visit the same websites in a different language setting, you will see a different format. answer: across cultures from left to right from top to bottom adjust
